title: Sheinbaum Backs Chiapas Coffee Growers: “Nestlé Must Pay a Fair Price”
author: Redacción/SinEmbargo
content:
_This article
by[Redacción/SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/)
originally appeared in the [November 25, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4909889/sheinbaum-respalda-a-
cafeticultores-de-chiapas-nestle-tiene-que-pagar-lo-justo/), a Mexican digital
news outlet._

_The president announced that the Secretariat of Agriculture will support
Chiapas coffee growers seeking better payment for their harvests._

**Mexico City, November 25 (SinEmbargo).-** **President[Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/claudia-sheinbaum/)** expressed her
support this Wednesday for **coffee producers** in
[**Chiapas**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/estados/) who are demanding that
**Nestlé** pay more for their harvests, and stressed that the company must pay
a fair price.

Last Monday, **coffee growers** from about twenty **municipalities** in
**Chiapas** demonstrated in **Tapachula** to protest the company’s decision to
reduce its payment per kilo from 60 pesos to 43 pesos per kilo, directly
affecting around 165,000 families that produce these **beans**.

The protesting farmers said the fairest price would be 55 pesos per kilo, as
this would allow them to cover production costs and earn a reasonable profit.

In response, [President Sheinbaum](https://www.gob.mx/presidencia/) expressed
her support for coffee producers in Chiapas and stressed that the company must
pay a fair price for each kilo of beans.

> "I agree with the coffee growers. Nestlé has to pay what it has to pay for a
> kilo of coffee, because they are right. They say: 'it sells for 580 pesos
> and is bought for 43 pesos,' and they are asking that it continue to be
> bought for between 50 and 60 pesos, so we fully agree with what they are
> requesting," the president said during her morning press conference.

## Sheinbaum Promises to Support Chiapas Coffee Growers

In response to protests by coffee growers in Chiapas, President Claudia
Sheinbaum instructed the head of the Secretariat of Agriculture and Rural
Development (Sader), Columba López Gutiérrez, to travel to the state and
support coffee producers in negotiations with Nestlé.

The president also criticized the company for determining how much it pays
Mexican coffee producers based on international market prices, and questioned
why instant coffee prices do not fall when farmers are paid less.

> “It cannot be that the international market determines coffee prices for
> growers, even through intermediaries, because purchases are not made
> directly from them, while the price of Nescafé does not fall.”
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

For these reasons, the president insisted that “Nestlé has to pay and buy
directly from producers.”

Finally, Sheinbaum said she would discuss the issue with Chiapas Governor
Eduardo Ramírez Aguilar, with whom she will meet this Wednesday at the
National Palace, in the context of her meeting with members of Section VII of
the National Coordinating Committee of Education Workers (CNTE).
